calculationDraft:
Correct: Energy cannot be created or destroyed, only converted from one form to another. 
   Distractor A (Computational Error): Thinking energy is created when it's actually converted (e.g., burning gasoline creates energy).
   Distractor B (Conceptual Misconception): Believing energy can be destroyed (e.g., energy is lost when a car brakes).
   Distractor C (Trap): Assuming energy conversion is 100% efficient (e.g., all energy from gasoline is converted into motion).
